quote: OLFM4 mRNA and protein were significantly upregulated in inflamed CD (4.3 and 1.7-fold) and even more pronounced in UC (24.8 and 3.7-fold).
summary: OLFM4 mRNA and protein are strongly upregulated in inflamed UC colon (24.8-fold mRNA) and Crohn's, and secreted into mucus.

quote: In addition, a colon barrier experiment revealed that epithelial cell proliferation of the mucus layer (Lgr5, Cyclin D1, and Olfm4) was downregulated and tight junction proteins (claudin-1 and ZO-1) were upregulated.
summary: Olfm4 is one of three proliferation markers downregulated by corylin in a mouse colitis-associated cancer model.

quote: These results show that Olfm4 deletion can successfully enhance immune defense against S. aureus, but not A. fumigatus, in CGD mice.
summary: Olfm4 deletion improved bacterial clearance and sepsis resistance in a mouse chronic granulomatous disease model; an infection setting, not colitis.

quote: The OLFM4-expressing PC-3 cell clones were found to have decreased proliferation and invasiveness compared with vector-transfected control PC-3 cells in vitro.
summary: OLFM4 overexpression reduced prostate cancer cell growth, invasion and tumor spread in mice; cancer setting with no inflammation outcome.

quote: Gene deletion of Cldn7 in intestines showed significant alteration of expression profiles with striking down-regulation of intestinal crypt stem cell markers such as Olfm4, dislocated proliferative cells, and disrupted epithelial cell differentiation.
summary: Olfm4 is a stem cell marker that falls in Cldn7-deficient intestine; the study concerns claudin-7.

quote: Chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1), CD38 molecule (CD38), and olfactomedin 4 (OLFM4) were upregulated in patients with CD or UC, whereas intelectin 1 (ITLN1) was downregulated.
summary: Proteomics of intestinal tissue found OLFM4 protein increased in both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis versus controls.

quote: Gene expression analyses in both cohorts identified Olfactomedin4 (OLFM4) as a fully discriminative marker between children with mild and severe RSV infection, giving a PAM cross-validation error of 0%.
summary: Blood OLFM4 expression discriminated mild from severe RSV infection in children; not an IBD study.

quote: Studies using OLFM4-deficient mouse models have revealed that OLFM4 acts as a negative regulator of H. pylori-specific immune responses and plays an important role in mucosal defense in inflammatory bowel disease.
summary: Mini-review of OLFM4 in digestive diseases: upregulated in IBD tissue and gastrointestinal cancers, with a negative regulatory role in immune responses.

quote: We performed analysis of CHD7 in 36 patients with KS and 20 patients with normosmic idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (nIHH) in whom mutations in KAL1, FGFR1, PROK2 and PROKR2 genes were excluded.
summary: PROK2 is named only as one of several genes excluded for mutations in a CHD7 Kallmann syndrome study.

quote: Antibodies blocking G-CSF, or its target Bv8/PROK2, suppressed tumor progression and myeloid cell infiltration when combined with anti-VEGF in CIC-associated CRC and in anti-VEGF-resistant CRC liver metastasis models.
summary: Blocking Bv8/PROK2 with antibody, with anti-VEGF, suppressed colitis-associated colorectal tumors and myeloid infiltration in mice; high plasma levels linked to worse survival.
Verotoxin binding to P blood group antigens on erythrocytes; no relation to the PROK2 gene.

quote: In vivo, Compound 3 reversed intracolonic mustard oil-induced referred allodynia and TNBS-induced visceral hypersensitivity, but not non-inflammatory, stress-induced visceral pain.
summary: Prok2 is upregulated in UC biopsies and rodent colitis; a prokineticin receptor antagonist reversed inflammatory visceral pain, suggesting PROK2 signaling inhibition may help.

quote: In mouse models, PK2 over-expression aggravated psoriasis while its knock-down inhibited pathological development.
summary: PK2 over-expression worsened and knock-down reduced psoriasis in mice via an IL-1 feedback loop; a skin study, not colitis.

quote: In tandem, arbutin suppressed the testicular NLRP3/caspase-1/NF-B axis and augmented the cytoprotective PK2/PKR2 pathway.
summary: Arbutin raised the PK2/PKR2 pathway in lead-injured rat testis among several pathways; no gene-specific perturbation and not a UC study.

quote: ConclusionsPK2 inhibition suppressed arthritis in mice with CIA.
summary: The PK2 antagonist PKRA7 reduced arthritis severity in collagen-induced arthritis mice; not a colitis model.

quote: Prokineticin 2 (Prok2) mRNA, a cytokine-like molecule associated with gastrointestinal tract inflammation, was significantly down-regulated in ethanol-fed mice.
summary: Prok2 mRNA was reduced in ethanol-fed mice and correlated with gut bacterial genera; an alcohol liver study, not colitis.

quote: A total of 13 crosstalk genes (IL1B, CSF3, CXCL1, CXCL6, FPR1, FCGR3B, SELE, MMP7, PROK2, SRGN, FCN1, TDO2 and CYP24A1) were identified via DEGs analysis and WGCNA by combining PD and CD data sets.
summary: PROK2 is one of 13 crosstalk genes shared by periodontitis and Crohn's disease transcriptomes, without gene-specific analysis.

quote: Once PK2 is released in inflamed tissue, it is involved in both innate and adaptive responses: it triggers macrophage recruitment, production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and reduction of anti-inflammatory cytokines.
summary: Review of prokineticins in neuroinflammation, including gastrointestinal inflammation, describing PK2 as pro-inflammatory.

quote: However, two had been previously proposed in adult inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), namely, MMP9 and PROK2.
summary: PROK2 emerged as a candidate biomarker overlapping between colonic biopsies and blood in pediatric UC expression meta-analysis.

quote: Machine learning identified LCN2, REG1A, AQP9, CCL2, GIP, PROK2, DEFA5, CXCL9, and NAMPT; AQP9, PROK2, LCN2, and NAMPT were further verified by ROC curves and IHC in the external cohort.
summary: PROK2 was selected by machine learning as a Crohn's disease diagnostic biomarker and verified by ROC and immunohistochemistry.

quote: We found that adult CORT-nursed rats, in comparison to controls, showed increased expression of colonic GR and reduced expression of pro-inflammatory molecules (IL-1β, TNF-α, PK2 and PK2L) in response to inflammatory colitis.
summary: Colonic PK2 was lower in colitis-protected CORT-nursed rats after TNBS than in controls.

quote: The goal of the present study was to determine the effects of mild moxibustion on the expression of PK2 and PKR2 in colon and spinal cord in IBS rat model, which was induced by colorectal distension using inflatable balloons.
summary: PK2 and PKR2 were raised in colon and spinal cord of IBS rats and reduced by moxibustion; an IBS pain model, not UC.

quote: Our data suggest that the AOX diet may alter IL6 signaling following GR and completely block the expression of the prokineticin PROK2, the ligand to the G protein-coupled receptors PROKR1 and PROKR2, which are involved in a number of pathophysiological processes.
summary: An antioxidant diet blocked Prok2 expression after radiation in mice; a radiation study, not colitis.

quote: In addition, there are dramatic increases in the TLR4, MyD88, NF-κB, and PK2/PKR1 protein expression levels.
summary: PK2/PKR1 protein rose in LPS-induced rat orchitis and oxytocin mitigated the damage; not a UC study.

quote: Rare heterozygous PROK2/R2 variants contribute to known reproductive and novel gastrointestinal phenotypes within a hospital-based population cohort.
summary: Rare PROK2/PROKR2 variant carriers had more lower gastrointestinal phenotypes in a recall-by-genotype cohort, without a stated direction or UC link.
